CRM and marketing: contacts, companies, deals, tickets and more in one HubSpot account.

**Ways to connect:** API key, connect accounts.

## API key

- **Get your key here:** [developers.hubspot.com](https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/apps/legacy-apps/private-apps/overview)
- **Setting:** `HUBSPOT_API_TOKEN`
- **API reference:** [developers.hubspot.com](https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/api-reference/latest/overview)

### Get the key

1. Sign in to HubSpot and open [developers.hubspot.com](https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/apps/legacy-apps/private-apps/overview).
2. Create an API key (or token) with only the access your apps need.
3. Copy it. Many providers show a key only once.

**What to create:** An access token from a HubSpot legacy private app (Development > Legacy apps > Create legacy app > Private), scoped to what the app needs; the Gateway sends it as a bearer token. CRM search is a POST, so an app that searches needs write access.

Steps for this provider are brief. [Open an issue](https://github.com/every-app/every-app/issues/new?template=provider-request.yml&title=Provider%20guide%3A%20HubSpot) to request a full guide.

### Set it on your Gateway

From your EveryApp folder:

```bash
everyapp secret set HUBSPOT_API_TOKEN
```

It asks for the value at a hidden prompt, and it's live at once, with no deploy. If an app you've installed needs it, `everyapp configure <app>` asks for it along with everything else the app needs.

### Use it in an app

List it in the app's `everyapp.config.ts`:

```ts
capabilities: {
  hubspot: { access: "read", why: "What the app does with it." },
},
```

`access` is `"read"` (or `"write"` where it changes things). The app calls the provider's own URLs with `integrationFetch()`, and the Gateway adds the key. More in [API providers](/docs/agent/providers).

### Check it worked

- `everyapp provider show hubspot` shows the key as set and which apps use it.
- `everyapp status` shows apps that were waiting for it as ready.
- To test the key itself, `GET https://api.hubapi.com/account-info/2026-09/details` with it should answer 200; the call is free.

### Cost and limits

- **Rate limits:** 250000 a day. Private apps on Free and Starter: 100 per 10 seconds per app and 250,000 a day per account; Pro 190 and 625,000; Enterprise 190 and 1,000,000.

## Connect accounts

Each person connects their own HubSpot account once, in the Gateway, and every app that asks for it uses that connection. Apps never see the tokens. [How connecting works](/docs/connect-oauth)

- **Make the OAuth app here:** [developers.hubspot.com](https://developers.hubspot.com/)
- **Settings:** `HUBSPOT_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`, `HUBSPOT_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`
- **Added with:** `everyapp provider add --oauth hubspot-oauth`

### Redirect URI

Register this at the provider:

```text
https://<your gateway>/connect/hubspot-oauth/callback
```

`<your gateway>` is your Gateway's address, like `apps.example.com`.

An app that runs the sign-in itself lists its own callbacks under `redirectPaths` in its manifest entry; register those too, as `https://<app>.<your gateway><path>`. `everyapp provider show hubspot-oauth` prints every one.

### Make the OAuth app

The app's scopes in HubSpot's developer console must match the sets apps declare, or HubSpot refuses the authorize URL.

1. Open [developers.hubspot.com](https://developers.hubspot.com/) and create an OAuth app (sometimes called a client or an integration).
2. Add the redirect URI above.
3. Allow the scopes behind the sets your apps use (the table below), and no others.
4. Copy the client ID and the client secret. The secret is often shown once.

Steps for this provider are brief. [Open an issue](https://github.com/every-app/every-app/issues/new?template=provider-request.yml&title=Provider%20guide%3A%20HubSpot) to request a full guide.

### Set it on your Gateway

From your EveryApp folder:

```bash
everyapp provider add --oauth hubspot-oauth
everyapp secret set HUBSPOT_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID HUBSPOT_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET
```

Each value goes in at a hidden prompt. Or, as an owner or admin, paste the client in **Manage workspace → Providers → Add OAuth provider**.

### Scope sets

Apps ask for named sets, never raw scopes, and the Gateway holds each app to the sets it declared.

| Set | Allows | Provider scopes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `contacts.read` | Contacts (read) | `crm.objects.contacts.read` |
| `contacts.write` | Contacts (read and write) | `crm.objects.contacts.read`, `crm.objects.contacts.write` |
| `companies.read` | Companies (read) | `crm.objects.companies.read` |
| `deals.read` | Deals (read) | `crm.objects.deals.read` |

### Use it in an app

```ts
capabilities: {
  "hubspot-oauth": { access: "read", scopes: ["contacts.read"], why: "What the app does with it." },
},
```

### Check it worked

- `everyapp provider show hubspot-oauth` shows the client as set, and the redirect URI.
- Open the account menu → **Connected accounts** → **Connect HubSpot**. You land back in the Gateway, connected.
- `everyapp provider connections` lists who has connected.
